results.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views | alphaXiv
results.content:
## Testing the alternative

The obvious skeptical question is whether letting points move would do better. The authors test learned positional offsets with the geometry backbone frozen, using pre-refinement averages over 4, 8, and 16 input views on ETH3D and DTU. Offsets worsen both metrics on both datasets: ETH3D LPIPS is 0.4998 with offsets versus 0.4339 for the main method, and DTU is 0.2826 versus 0.2070. Fine-tuning the geometry branch rather than freezing it also worsens both metrics on these two datasets, while ground-truth-camera back-projection and large-angle supervision each improve both relative to their alternatives. These are ablations on two datasets, and they do not show that geometry error is the only source of artifacts.

## What opacity learns [...] ## The headline result

The main comparison is the feed-forward, pose-conditioned output, averaged over six evaluation datasets. Each example has four held-out target views, inputs are 4, 8, or 16 views, and results are averaged equally over input counts within a dataset and then equally across datasets. LPIPS and DISTS, both perceptual-distance metrics where lower is better, are the primary quality measures. Mean LPIPS is 0.2472 versus 0.3333 for ReSplat, the strongest evaluated baseline on that metric, and mean DISTS is 0.1163 versus 0.1734 for WorldMirror 2.0, the strongest on that metric. The authors report these as reductions of 25.8% and 32.9%. These are rendering-quality gains, not measurements of speed.

## Testing the alternative [...] Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free

# InfiniSplat Moves from Single-Image to Multi-View 3DGS Reconstruction

Explore InfiniSplat's single-image and multi-view workflows, the code, model weights and demos available to try.

KIRI Team · Oct 16, 2026

InfiniSplat is a feed-forward reconstruction workflow for novel-view rendering from the research group ZJU3DV. V1 turns a single image into an explorable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scene, designed to maintain more coherent spatial structure as the viewpoint changes. The updated V2 extends this workflow to multiple photographs of the same scene, reconstructing a 3D Gaussian scene that can be explored from new viewpoints.

## InfiniSplat: Exploring a Scene from One Photograph [...] InfiniSplat V1 demo showing a single bedroom photograph on the left and its reconstructed 3D Gaussian scene on the right, with black gaps around unobserved scene boundaries./webresources/Blog/infinisplat-1.png "InfiniSplat V1 reconstructs an explorable 3D Gaussian scene from a single photograph, enabling novel-view rendering.")InfiniSplat V1: Single-Image 3D Gaussian Splatting Reconstruction

## V2: Multiple Views and Cleaner Gaussian Rendering

InfiniSplat v2 adds overlapping photographs of the same scene, providing observations beyond a single viewpoint. It supports supplied camera poses and intrinsics, or reconstruction without supplied camera parameters. [...] Built on Depth Anything 3, InfiniSplat v2 addresses a problem with converting predicted geometry into renderable Gaussians: point clouds can contain floating or inconsistent points. The method freezes its geometry branch and trains a separate branch to predict Gaussian attributes. In particular, learned opacity allows unreliable points to contribute less to the final rendering. Rather than requiring every imperfect point to be corrected geometrically, the model can reduce the visual impact of inconsistent geometry when producing new views.

### TL;DR

 InfiniSplat is a feed-forward single-image 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for large-baseline novel view synthesis.
 It moves Gaussian generation from pixel-aligned image grids toward surface-aligned supports guided by monocular geometry.
 A query-conditioned implicit Gaussian decoder predicts Gaussian attributes on sampled supports, producing more coherent surfaces under large viewpoint changes.
